newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cautious Brussels bourse seen more volatile.
newsitem.headline: Cautious Brussels bourse seen more volatile.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended a cautious and thinly traded Wednesday with slight gains after New York failed to follow through on record overnight gains, and traders said they expected a period of greater volatility.
"Everybody was astounded by the strong gains in the Dow on Tuesday. In Europe we were much more cautious and we did not follow," one trader said.

The failure to build on the Dow's 135-point overnight gain and the slight weakening of the dollar combined to pour cold water on any latent optimism in Europe, leaving the Belgian market dithering uncertainly, traders noted.
"I think the market will become more volatile, particularly on the downside," a trader said.
He added that he expected the blue chip Bel-20 share index to look for support around the 2,000-points level over the coming weeks and months.
"That would be a good level to buy," he said.
Other traders were slightly more optimistic, seeing good support around 2,100 points.
The Bel-20 ended Wednesday up 4.09 points or just 0.19 percent at 2,133.60 having moved in a 2,142.60/2,130.40 range. Just over two billion francs of Belgian shares were traded.
Traders said there was no particular focus, although cyclical stocks were more in favour than financials.
"That is quite normal," one trader said. "Financials are out of favour, so cyclicals are in. But with long rates moving down, financials might start to come back again."
Main gainer among index stocks was chemicals and drugs firm UCB, up 2.1 percent at 91,750 francs in what traders said was a technical correction after recent relative weakness.
Oil major PetroFina, the busiest share by value, climbed 1.8 percent to 12,775 francs on followthrough after Tuesday's strong 4.6 percent rise.
